title: Record collection and praise for a New Orleans drummer
summary: Sal says he had a large record collection, Raymond came to hear it, and he praises a New Orleans drummer as the best.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Well, I do. As a matter of fact, I had a lot of records. Raymond Boyd, you know, Raymond Will. I've known Raymond for years. He's come around my house. He says, you got some nice records in town? I said, yeah, I had a record box. Big Spider-Bank, Wolverine Band, Tylan Blues, Roy Gordon, all those records. He's come to my house, see. I said, big record box full of records, see, and arranged to come around and hear my records, see. I go to his house, see. And you know, I thought that doesn't get any recognition in the jazz club. And the class I was saying to me that I'm the only man she ever heard praising other drum, see. That's the way I am. God's good, he's good, see. To me, they got the top drum in New Orleans, boy. I live at it.
I've heard many, many musicians say that, and I don't think that the general public understood what he was doing. Very tough, man. Tops.
